clonoview_bundle

Source: R/clonoview.R
clonoview_bundle.Rd

Prepare a Clonotrace run for viewing in ClonoView.

Usage

clonoview_bundle(
  cell_embedding,
  cell_meta,
  clone_cluster,
  cell_profile_prob,
  name,
  label = name,
  clone_column = "clone",
  cell_type_column = NULL,
  patient_column = NULL,
  visit_column = NULL,
  patient_fields = NULL,
  clone_id_regex = NULL,
  patient_default = "sample",
  visits = NULL,
  visit_labels = NULL,
  visit_aliases = NULL,
  kind = NULL,
  notes = "",
  expanded_min = NULL,
  python = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

cell_embedding

Cell embedding: a data frame or matrix with cells in rows, identified by row names or a `cell` column, and two coordinate columns.

cell_meta

Per-cell table, cells in rows, identified by row names or a `cell` column. Must contain `clone_column`.

clone_cluster

Clone embedding and profile assignment, as returned by [leiden_dis()] with `if_umap = TRUE`: clones in rows, with coordinates and a `cluster` column.

cell_profile_prob

Cell-by-profile probability matrix, with cells as row names and profile numbers as column names. Sparse matrices are accepted.

name

Short identifier for the dataset; becomes the bundle's directory name.

label

Human-readable name shown in the viewer. Defaults to `name`.

clone_column

Column of `cell_meta` holding the clone assignment.

cell_type_column

Column of `cell_meta` holding the cell-type annotation.

patient_column, visit_column

Columns of `cell_meta` holding patient and visit.

patient_fields

Named character vector of further per-patient columns to show, as `c("Display name" = "column_name")`.

clone_id_regex

Python regular expression parsing the clone identifier, naming any of the groups `patient`, `visit`, `receptor`. See details.

patient_default

Sample name used when clone identifiers carry no patient.

visits

Visit codes in sampling order. Defaults to the sorted unique values of `visit_column`, or a single visit if there is none.

visit_labels

Named character vector, visit code to display label.

visit_aliases

Named character vector mapping the spelling used in `cell_meta` onto the code used in the clone identifier, as `c("Baseline" = "B")`.

kind

`"sequence"` for a time course, `"pre_post"` for numbered biopsies that are not successive visits, `"single"` for one timepoint. Inferred if not given.

notes

Free text shown in the viewer's dataset header.

expanded_min

The cell threshold the run used to call a clone expanded, recorded so the viewer can say how many cells fell below it.

python

Python interpreter to use. Defaults to [clonoview_python()].

verbose

Whether to print progress.

Value

The dataset name, invisibly.

Details

Takes the objects a Clonotrace run leaves in the session, writes them out in the layout ClonoView reads, and compiles them into a bundle. Run it once per dataset; [clonoview()] then serves whatever has been bundled.

The four required arguments are the four things the viewer draws:

`cell_embedding`

the cell UMAP, as passed to [dimplot()]

`cell_meta`

the per-cell table, which must carry the clone assignment

`clone_cluster`

the [leiden_dis()] result – clone coordinates and the profile each clone belongs to

`cell_profile_prob`

the cell-by-profile probability matrix

Everything else describes study design, and all of it is optional. With none of it supplied the run is treated as a single sample with no time dimension, which is the right reading of a lineage-barcoding experiment: there is one library, and the viewer's time control correctly has one step.

Sample structure lives in the clone identifier. A clone in a longitudinal study is a clone at one timepoint, so which patient and which visit a clone belongs to has to be recoverable from its name. `clone_id_regex` is how, and it must name the groups it extracts: with clone identifiers spelled `p12|Baseline|CASSLGQAYEQYF`, `clone_id_regex = "^(?P<patient>[^|]+)\\|(?P<visit>[^|]+)\\|(?P<receptor>.+)$"` splits them. Any of the three groups may be left out; omit the argument entirely and the clone identifier is taken whole, as one lineage in one sample.

The `patient_column` and `visit_column` arguments say where the cell table records the same facts. They are what puts a cell in the patient table, and they are independent of the regex: cells that carry no clone still have a patient.

See also

[clonoview()], [clonoview_datasets()]

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# after the clone embedding and profile steps of the vignette
clonoview_bundle(cell_embedding = umap,
                 cell_meta = cell_meta,
                 clone_cluster = clone_cluster,
                 cell_profile_prob = cell_profile_prob,
                 name = "hematopoiesis",
                 cell_type_column = "Cell.type.annotation")
clonoview("hematopoiesis")
} # }
